newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan April trade deficit US$203.5 mln.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan April trade deficit US$203.5 mln.

text.p: Taiwan had a trade deficit of US$203.5 million in April, compared with April 1996's surplus of US$845 million, the finance ministry said on Wednesday.
Exports in March totalled US$9.84 billion, down 2.5 percent from April 1996, the ministry said.
Imports rose an annual 8.6 percent to US$10.043, marking the second consecutive month that imports had surpassed US$10 billion.
The April deficit was close to the average forecast for a deficit of US$166 million compiled from a Reuters poll of Taiwan economists on May 2.
The economists also predicted that exports would total US$10.148 billion and imports would be US$10.314 billion.
Hsu Kuo-chung, the ministry's chief statistician, attributed the decline in exports to an all-out export ban on pork following Taiwan's hog foot-and-disease epidemic in March.
"Not counting the losses on pork, exports would have been down only about 1.3 percent," Hsu told reporters.
Before the ban, Taiwan had been exporting about US$130 million worth of pork per month.
Hsu said the export fall also was due to a higher base in April 1996 that resulted from scheduled exports in March 1996 being delayed one month due to military tensions between Taiwan and China.

The ministry attributed the high imports mainly to a hefty US$387 million military outlay arising partly from the import of the first two of six Lafayette-class missile frigates purchased from France.

April exports to the United States rose 8.3 percent to US$2.364 billion from US$2.182 billion in April 1996.
Hong Kong was the next biggest destination with exports totalling US$2.353 billion, down 0.2 percent from US$2.358 billion in April 1996.

Japan remained Taiwan's top import source, accounting for US$2.584 billion or 25.7 percent of the total, followed by the United States at US$2.002 billion (19.9 percent) and Europe at US$1.810 billion (18 percent).
The April trade surplus with Hong Kong, which serves as the main conduit for Taiwan's lucrative and growing trade with rival China, remained the largest by far at US$2.186 billion.
Taiwan's trade deficit with Japan was US$1.611 billion.
-- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
